findings.title: Keep the booked discount after its live promotion is deleted
findings.issue: The saved booking snapshot is used only when promotion_id is truthy. Deleting an offer is supported, and the existing FK sets appointment.promotion_id to NULL while leaving the saved selected service and discount snapshots. On later consultation finalization or draft save, this helper removes the booked discount and raises the patient total.
findings.evidence: Synthetic post-delete state: service 400, saved discount 100; before live ID is cleared the discount is 100, afterwards it is 0 and the bill becomes 400 instead of 300. No live row was deleted.
findings.fix: Treat a valid saved booking snapshot as authoritative independently of the optional live promotion FK. Apply current offer eligibility only to added-service selections. Add a booked-offer-deletion regression.
findings.confidence: Reproduced with actual helper and in-memory query executor.

findings.title: Interpret SMS quota timestamps in the database timezone
findings.issue: The connection returns DATETIME strings (dateStrings:true) and defaults to +08:00, but new Date(row.window_start/last_sent_at) parses a timezone-free string in the Node host timezone. On a UTC host, the stored timestamps appear eight hours in the future: cooldown is skipped and the hourly window becomes nine hours.
findings.evidence: In a UTC process with MySQL-style +08:00 strings, attempts at 0, 1 and 2 seconds were all allowed. Attempt 4 at 3 seconds returned retryAfterSeconds=32397 instead of enforcing the first 60-second pause. The current unit mock stores Date objects and misses this boundary.
findings.fix: Use a single explicit timezone/UTC representation or database-native time comparisons for the entire quota window. Test mysql2 dateStrings values on a UTC host.
findings.confidence: Reproduced with actual quota code and synthetic dateStrings executor.

findings.title: Give each confirmation event its own email idempotency key
findings.issue: Every confirmation for an appointment uses doctor-confirm-<id>. A patient can reschedule an already confirmed appointment back to pending; when the clinic confirms again, the changed date/time produces a new email payload with the old key.
findings.evidence: Captured two actual helper payloads for appointment 9 on different dates/times: both keys were doctor-confirm-9 and the HTML differed. No email was sent. Provider rejection is an inference from the documented API contract.
findings.fix: Key by a persisted confirmation-event/revision identifier, retaining the same key only for retries of that exact event.
findings.confidence: Key/payload collision reproduced locally; delivery behavior verified from official documentation.

findings.title: Update migration-order expectations for the three appended migrations
findings.issue: The runner appends registration-sms-limits, billing-stock-reservations and doctor-confirmation-notifications, but the pinned-check test still asserts the old last five files. This makes the existing backend regression suite fail deterministically.
findings.evidence: The current checked-in migration SQL matches pinned SHA-256 checksums test now fails. The displayed diff is the expected migration tail, not a changed historical SQL hash.
findings.fix: Assert the updated complete registration order/tail while retaining historical hash and replay/type/history checks. Do not change old migration SQL or delete failing tests.
findings.confidence: Observed in the fresh full backend Node run.
